label: early original-phase steps (t=1,2) after a "v" input
explanation: Fires only at original-phase steps t=1 and t=2 (99.8% of mass), and essentially only when a v has already been input: either v is the first token (t=1, activation about 0.64-0.72 of max), or v is at step 0 or 1 and this is step 2. prev_tok==v alone has precision 1.0 and covers 89% of mass. The strongest activations (about 1.0 of max) come at t=2 for sequences starting v v, or v followed by certain tokens such as r or s. Some step-2 cases after v at step 0 stay silent (e.g. v 0 y, v o e), and these are most of the false positives. Missed activations are tiny near-zero firings after u/j/s first tokens, worth 0.3% of mass. Does not fire at t=0, at t>=3, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (139 negligible steps).

issues: The explanation says prev_tok==v alone has precision 1.0. That is false: on the test split it scores precision 0.186 (recall 0.545, mass recall 0.89). Precision is 1.0 only once you restrict to (phase==0)&isin(t,[1,2]).

The explanation says the strongest activations include 'v followed by certain tokens such as r or s'. 'v r' is wrong: at t=2 with orig(0)=v and orig(1)=r the feature is completely silent (precision 0.0). 's' is correct (precision 1.0).

The false positives are not scattered. Every one of them (4607 on test) is a single fixed class: t=2, orig(0)=v, orig(1) in {f,g,o,p,r,z,0,2}. For each of those second tokens precision is 0.0. For every other second token after a leading v, precision is 1.0.
The 'v v' sequences that the explanation calls the strongest case hold only 2.2% of activation mass. The main mass sits on t=1 after a leading v (46%) and on t=2 when v is at step 1 (41%).

Checks that hold up: phase/t localisation is correct (t=1 and t=2 carry 99.8% of mass; t=0, the delimiter and t>=4 are silent; there are 139 negligible copy-phase steps and 433 negligible steps at t=3). The misses are many tiny activations (0.00-0.03 of max) after other first tokens (u, j, s, e, m, a), worth 0.3% of mass and each with low precision. That is diffuse weak noise, not a meaningful class.
The label 'after a v input' is broadly right, but the predicate seen(v) overclaims: it includes the deterministic silent class.
skeptic.revised_label: original-phase t=1/t=2 steps right after a "v" input (t=2 after a leading v only when the second token is not one of f,g,o,p,r,z,0,2)
